docx_script = '''import openpyxl
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from collections import Counter

# 1. Read inventory data
wb = openpyxl.load_workbook("testbed/data/product_inventory.xlsx")
ws = wb["Products"]

products = []
for row in ws.iter_rows(min_row=2, max_row=ws.max_row, values_only=True):
    products.append({
        "id": row[0],
        "name": row[1],
        "category": row[2],
        "price": row[3],
        "in_stock": row[4],
    })

# 2. Compute summary stats
total_products = len(products)
categories = Counter(p["category"] for p in products)
prices = [p["price"] for p in products if p["price"] is not None]
total_value = sum(prices)
avg_price = total_value / len(prices) if prices else 0
min_price = min(prices) if prices else 0
max_price = max(prices) if prices else 0
all_in_stock = all(str(p["in_stock"]).strip().lower() == "yes" for p in products)

# 3. Build Word document
doc = Document()

# Title
title = doc.add_heading("Product Inventory Summary", level=0)
title.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER

# Overview paragraph
doc.add_heading("Overview", level=1)
overview = doc.add_paragraph()
overview.add_run("Source file: ").bold = True
overview.add_run("testbed/data/product_inventory.xlsx\\n")
overview.add_run("Total products: ").bold = True
overview.add_run(f"{total_products}\\n")
overview.add_run("Stock status: ").bold = True
overview.add_run(f"All {total_products} listed items are marked In Stock as Yes.\\n")
overview.add_run("Price range: ").bold = True
overview.add_run(f"${min_price} \\u2013 ${max_price}\\n")
overview.add_run("Average price: ").bold = True
overview.add_run(f"${avg_price:.2f}\\n")
overview.add_run("Total catalog value: ").bold = True
overview.add_run(f"${total_value}")

# Category breakdown
doc.add_heading("Category Breakdown", level=1)
cat_table = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=2, style="Light List Accent 1")
cat_table.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
hdr = cat_table.rows[0].cells
hdr[0].text = "Category"
hdr[1].text = "Number of Products"
for cat, count in sorted(categories.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
    row = cat_table.add_row().cells
    row[0].text = str(cat)
    row[1].text = str(count)

# Full product listing
doc.add_heading("Full Product Listing", level=1)
note = doc.add_paragraph()
note.add_run("Note: ").bold = True
note.add_run("All listed items are marked In Stock as Yes.")

prod_table = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=5, style="Light List Accent 1")
prod_table.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
hdr = prod_table.rows[0].cells
hdr[0].text = "Product ID"
hdr[1].text = "Name"
hdr[2].text = "Category"
hdr[3].text = "Price"
hdr[4].text = "In Stock"
for p in products:
    row = prod_table.add_row().cells
    row[0].text = str(p["id"])
    row[1].text = str(p["name"])
    row[2].text = str(p["category"])
    row[3].text = f"${p['price']}"
    row[4].text = str(p["in_stock"])

# Adjust column widths for readability
for row in prod_table.rows:
    row.cells[0].width = Inches(1.3)
    row.cells[1].width = Inches(2.5)
    row.cells[2].width = Inches(1.1)
    row.cells[3].width = Inches(0.7)
    row.cells[4].width = Inches(0.7)

# Save
output_path = "testbed/data/inventory_summary.docx"
doc.save(output_path)
print(f"Document saved to {output_path}")
print(f"Total products: {total_products}")
print(f"Categories: {dict(categories)}")
print(f"All in stock: {all_in_stock}")
